title: Sales enablement playbook: positioning, competitive briefs, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ
author: Elena Martínez
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook equips Redwood sales and solutions teams with positioning, competitive brief material, pitch-deck guidance, pricing guidance, example case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospects evaluating inference platforms. Use this as the canonical reference for customer conversations and enablement assets.

Audience: AEs, solutions engineers, SDRs, customer success managers, and marketing enablement contributors.

Contact: Elena Martínez (Go-to-Market) — elena@redwood.ai; for technical deep-dive requests loop in Marcus Liu (Solutions Engineering).

---

1) Executive positioning and elevator pitches

Short elevator pitch (20s): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLM-powered features predictable and economical in production — across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — by combining a GPU-optimized serving runtime, smart routing, and observability tuned for production SLAs.

Problem statement (what prospects feel): Teams building product features with LLMs struggle to meet latency and cost targets, manage model rollouts safely, and get consistent performance between cloud and private deployments.

Core differentiators (one-liners):
- Production-first: predictable SLOs, transparent latency/cost metrics, and rollouts designed for production risk.
- Unified runtime: same API and tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Cost controls: batching, caching, and quantization guidance that materially reduce per-token spend.

Key buyer personas and tailored messages:
- ML/Infra/Platform Engineers: Emphasize observability, per-route token/latency breakdown, model variant fallback, and autoscaling controls.
- Product/Feature Teams: Emphasize ease-of-use, fast onboarding, and consistent behavior across environments.
- Security/Compliance/IT: Emphasize private deployment options, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and SOC2 evidence.

---

2) Value proposition by product capability

- Redwood API (hosted): Fast time-to-value, usage-based pricing, streaming, function/tool calling, and transparent performance profiles.
- Redwood Dedicated: Reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, latency SLAs, and configurable autoscaling/burst capacity.
- Redwood Private: VPC and on-prem deployment options, customer-managed network, KMS/HSM support, and audit logging.
- Redwood Console: Token-level cost and latency dashboards, per-route tracing, rollout controls, and regression alerts tied to evals.
- Redwood Optimize: Actionable batching/quantization recommendations and quality steering to reduce unit costs with guardrails.

---

3) Competitive brief (high level)

Top competitors: Major cloud managed endpoints, LLM API providers, and inference infra vendors. Competitive themes and quick rebuttals:

- "We can self-host and save money": Rebuttal — self-hosted teams often underestimate ops cost and ongoing tuning. Redwood combines a tuned runtime plus operational tooling (rollouts, tracing, quality regressions) that reduces engineering time and TCO.
- "Other APIs are simpler/cheaper": Rebuttal — Redwood surfaces per-token and latency economics and provides recommendations to improve unit costs; for customers who prioritize SLAs and predictable throughput, Redwood Dedicated offers better total economic predictability.
- "We need full data isolation / on-prem": Rebuttal — Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packaging with audit evidence and KMS integrations; we can run a technical workshop and provide an architecture reference.

Competitive feature table (talking points):
- Model catalog and verified performance: Redwood maintains curated open models with verified latency/cost profiles for common sequence lengths.
- Rollouts and fallback: Canary, A/B testing, automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity constrained.
- Observability: Per-route token/latency/cost breakdown and eval-linked quality regression alerts.
- Cost controls: Automatic prefix/KV caching and batching config suggestions plus quantization recommendations.

Use case mapping:
- Startups prioritizing speed-to-market: Redwood API + Console for quick integration.
- Mid-market with growth: Transition to Dedicated for commit-backed predictability.
- Regulated enterprise: Private deployment with audit logs and KMS.

---

4) Pitch deck — recommended 10-slide outline (talk track snippets)

Slide 1: Title / Hook — "Ship predictable LLM features: lower latency, lower cost, less ops risk."
Slide 2: Problem — short bullets describing engineering, cost, reliability challenges.
Slide 3: Market opportunity — LLM features are table stakes for product differentiation.
Slide 4: Redwood solution overview — unified runtime, routing, caching, and deployment modes.
Slide 5: Demo / Architecture — sequence diagram: client -> Redwood API/edge -> serving runtime -> GPU pool / model variant -> response.
Slide 6: Performance and cost benchmarks — representative p50/p95 latencies, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens for popular models (use public benchmark slide from marketing).
Slide 7: Security & compliance — SOC2, VPC, on-prem, KMS, audit logs.
Slide 8: Customer stories — two brief case study bullets (metrics below).
Slide 9: Pricing options & example ROI calculation — hosted vs dedicated vs private.
Slide 10: Next steps / skus / PO next actions — trial offer, technical workshop, eval plan.

Assets to attach: standard pitch deck .pptx, one-pager PDF, benchmark CSV, two short case-study slides, security FAQ doc. Owner: Marcus Liu (solutions engineering) for technical demo assets.

---

5) Pricing guidance (talking points and examples)

Principles: be transparent about unit economics; present hosted as low-friction entry, Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Private for compliance-sensitive customers. Always tie pricing to ROI (reduced latency -> conversion uplift, lower per-token cost -> reduced product margin leak).

Hosted (usage-based) — sample guide:
- Text generation: $0.045 per 1k prompt tokens, $0.09 per 1k generation tokens (example numbers, confirm current ratecard).
- Embeddings: $0.02 per 1k embedding units.
- Free trial credits and volume discounts for > $X/month.

Dedicated (reserved capacity) — sample model:
- Commit structure: monthly or annual GPU-hour/throughput commit with discounted per-token rates when above thresholds.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime, p95 latency targets for common sequence lengths.
- Add-on: burst capacity at pre-negotiated rates.

Private (VPC/on-prem) — pricing model: platform fee + deployment engineering + optional support tier. Provide ballpark TCO scenarios during discovery.

Example cost scenario (talking point):
- Prototype startup running 50M tokens / month: hosted plan recommended; estimate $2.5k–$6k/mo depending on prompt/generation ratio and caching effectiveness.
- Growing product with stable traffic requiring p95 latency 250ms: recommend Dedicated — we model expected throughput needs and show 20–50% lower unit costs vs hosted at scale plus SLA.

Sales negotiation tips: always involve pricing ops on non-standard discounts; for committed deals tie discounts to volume/term and consider packaging Optimize/observability add-ons.

---

6) Case studies (two short vignettes for pitch use)

Case study A — Conversational SaaS startup (public example):
- Challenge: User-facing chat features had p95 latency of ~850ms and high per-session cost, causing poor retention on mobile.
- Redwood intervention: Moved to Redwood API, enabled prefix caching and recommended batching and a quantized model variant for chat flows.
- Outcome: p95 latency reduced to 220ms, per-session inference spend dropped by ~3x, 12% lift in trial->paid conversion attributed to improved UX.
- Assets: 1-page case study, quote from Head of Product, performance CSV.

Case study B — Regulated finance customer (anonymized):
- Challenge: Required data residency, auditable access logs, and strict KMS controls; also needed predictable throughput for end-of-day batch scoring.
- Redwood intervention: Private deployment in customer VPC, HSM-backed key management, rollout plan with canary and automated rollback.
- Outcome: Achieved compliance audit evidence, reduced ops burden by 60% vs their prior self-hosted solution, and achieved cost parity while meeting SLA targets.
- Assets: security-architecture diagram, compliance checklist, executive summary.

---

7) Security FAQ for prospects (short answers for sales conversations)

Q: Do you have third-party security certifications?
A: Yes — Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II (date/version) and is pursuing ISO 27001. For customer audits we provide the appropriate attestations through our security team.

Q: How is customer data protected at rest and in transit?
A: All traffic is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+). Data at rest is encrypted with customer-unique keys where applicable; for Private customers we integrate with customer KMS/HSM.

Q: Can we run Redwood fully on-prem / in our VPC?
A: Yes — we offer Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem packaging). On-prem engagements include an engineering integration phase and options for managed or co-managed operations.

Q: How do you handle audit logging and access controls?
A: We provide detailed audit logs for inference requests, admin actions, and model rollouts. RBAC and SSO integrations (OIDC/SAML) are supported and can be scoped per team.

Q: What is your vulnerability/patch cadence?
A: We maintain a regular security patch cadence for the control plane and publish patch windows for Private customers. Critical patches are treated with expedited timelines and communicated per our incident process.

Q: Do you support data residency / retention policies?
A: Yes — we host in multiple regions and can configure data residency for customer accounts. Retention policies can be configured per contract and are enforced in logs and storage.

Q: What about penetration testing and security reviews?
A: Redwood conducts annual pen tests and shares redacted reports with customers under NDA. We also support customer-led security assessments and provide an architecture review package.

Q: How do you protect model IP and customer prompts?
A: For Dedicated and Private customers we can isolate model storage and runtime. We do not use customer prompts to train public models and comply with contractual confidentiality terms.

---

8) Discovery checklist and standard demo plan (step-by-step)

Discovery checklist (questions to ask during initial discovery):
1) Primary persona and SLA needs: who owns latency and availability targets? (engineering/platform/product)
2) Expected qps and typical sequence lengths (prompt vs generation tokens).
3) Data sensitivity and residency requirements; any regulatory constraints.
4) Current stack: self-hosted, other API providers, model choices, and caching strategies.
5) Success criteria and timeline for POC/proof.
6) Budget and procurement constraints.

Standard demo plan (45-60 minutes):
1) 5 min — executive summary and objective alignment.
2) 20 min — technical deep-dive: runtime architecture, sample integration, performance dashboard walkthrough.
3) 10 min — security & compliance discussion for regulated customers.
4) 10 min — next steps: trial plan, metrics to measure, success criteria, and timeline.

Deliverables after demo: evaluation account, sample workload benchmark template (CSV), and 2-week POC plan with success metrics.

---

9) Objection handling (short playbook)

Objection: "We can do this ourselves and save money."
- Response: Acknowledge feasibility; focus on hidden costs: continuous kernel and runtime tuning, observability pipelines, rollout tooling, and regressions monitoring. Offer a TCO comparison workshop.

Objection: "We need strict data isolation / on-prem."
- Response: Explain Private deployment options, include a sample reference architecture and timeline, and propose an on-prem readiness checklist.

Objection: "Pricing is too high."
- Response: Show ROI examples, propose a small pilot/POC to demonstrate cost reductions from caching/quantization, and escalate to pricing ops for term-based discounts.
